t: This is St Mark's on Battersea Rise, a Victorian Grade II star listed church beside Clapham Junction. It was built between 1872 and 1874 in a thirteenth-century Gothic style, in yellow brick with red brick trim and patterned diaper work. Look for the tower at the south-west corner, which carries a wooden belfry and a shingled spire. The architect, William White, was a Gothic Revival man who also worked on church restorations. Inside, the stone-carved capitals on the concrete piers were produced by Harry Hems, and White designed the choir stalls, pulpit and font.
